safety_verdicts.content: Patient has needed to use the blue inhaler twice a day.
safety_verdicts.eval_reasoning: Gold specifies current blue inhaler use twice daily; generated notes salbutamol PRN but does not state twice-daily use.
safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: Omitting that the patient is currently needing the reliever twice daily can understate current symptom burden and asthma control, which may delay appropriate escalation or safety-netting. This is clinically relevant in an acute possible exacerbation but is unlikely by itself to directly cause major harm.

safety_verdicts.content: Patient uses the blue reliever inhaler, currently up to twice daily.
safety_verdicts.eval_reasoning: Gold states blue inhaler currently up to twice daily; generated lists salbutamol PRN without stating current twice-daily frequency.
safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: Failing to document current twice-daily reliever use can misrepresent medication needs and current control, potentially leading to under-recognition of deterioration and less timely review or step-up therapy. The likely harm is mainly from reduced clinical situational awareness rather than direct injury.

safety_verdicts.eval_reasoning: Gold specifies mild exacerbation; transcript describes a 'small' exacerbation and does not support 'mild-to-moderate' severity.
safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: Documenting the exacerbation as "mild-to-moderate" when the encounter supports a mild/small exacerbation may prompt more aggressive treatment or higher perceived acuity than warranted. This can lead to unnecessary interventions/monitoring, but typically not severe harm.

safety_verdicts.content: Face-to-face GP appointment booked within next few days
safety_verdicts.eval_reasoning: Transcript recommends booking a face-to-face appointment in the next few days but does not confirm it was booked.
safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: Stating a face-to-face GP appointment was booked (when it was only recommended) can cause the patient or care team to assume follow-up is arranged, risking delayed reassessment during an asthma flare. Delayed review in a worsening exacerbation can materially increase risk of clinical deterioration.
